title: Validate all objects in a work item
objective: Add sdlc work-item validate --work-item <work-item> to validate the selected work-item record and every task envelope and nested task payload declared by its stepsPath.

branch.name: main
branch.rationale: The repository is already on the main branch and the user requested preparation, processing of half the work item, and per-task commits on the current repository.

request.text:
Prepare a work item for sdlc work-item validate --work-item that validates all objects in the work item. commit the work item.

Process half of the new work-item, commit per task, then stop processing.

scope.name: work-item-validation-command
scope.description: Add sdlc work-item validate --work-item <work-item> as a read-only command that validates every object in the selected work-item artifact tree.
scope.reason: Operators need one command boundary to validate a complete work item rather than invoking separate schema checks manually.

scope.name: complete-object-coverage
scope.description: Validate work-item.json with work-item v2, every task envelope with task-envelope v1, and every nested task intent/result with its selected task schema.
scope.reason: A work item is an artifact tree whose task payloads may be structurally valid only when validated against their selected task contracts.

scope.name: validation-response
scope.description: Persist a closed response schema for complete, partial, and failed work-item object validation results.
scope.reason: CLI JSON response objects require durable versioned schemas and actionable per-object findings.

nonGoals.name: lifecycle-mutation
nonGoals.description: Do not change work-item or task lifecycle state, processingStatus, task results, or validation records while validating.
nonGoals.reason: The command is a read-only validation boundary.

nonGoals.name: semantic-approval
nonGoals.description: Do not approve, release, execute, repair, or semantically resolve the selected work item or its tasks.
nonGoals.reason: Schema/object validation is evidence of structural conformance, not approval or production readiness.

nonGoals.name: provider-and-production-runtime
nonGoals.description: Do not add provider calls, HTTP services, persistence, deployment, or production release behavior.
nonGoals.reason: WI-0010 is limited to local artifact discovery, schema validation, and response serialization.

items.name: complete-work-item-object-validation
items.description: sdlc work-item validate --work-item <work-item> must validate the selected work-item.json and every task envelope under its declared stepsPath.
items.reason: The command must cover the complete object tree represented by one work item.

acceptanceCriteria.description: The validator checks work-item.json against work-item v2 and each discovered YAML task envelope against task-envelope v1.
The validator checks each task intent and result against the task-specific schema selected by task.taskSchema, intentSchema, and resultSchema.

items.name: validation-response
items.description: The command must return a stable response identifying the work item, validation status, object counts, and per-object findings.
items.reason: Automation and operators need actionable results when one object in the artifact tree fails validation.

acceptanceCriteria.description: A persisted closed response schema covers valid, invalid, and operationally failed validation results with summary counts and object findings.
A fully valid work item returns exit code zero; any invalid object returns a non-zero result without mutating artifacts.

items.name: selector-and-read-only-boundary
items.description: The command must require --work-item <work-item>, preserve stable selector errors, and leave all validated files unchanged.
items.reason: Validation must be scoped, repeatable, and safe to run before processing or review.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Focused tests cover valid work-item validation, missing/duplicate/invalid/unknown selectors, malformed-object findings, and unchanged artifact bytes.

items.name: work-item-validation-evidence
items.description: The implementation must include representative validation of an existing complete work item and a fixture containing an invalid object.
items.reason: The command needs evidence for both complete success and actionable partial failure behavior.

acceptanceCriteria.description: yarn test and fresh-process work-item validation checks pass for a valid work item and an invalid temporary artifact tree.
